quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Only a certified mechanic can do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A pre-ride inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.
Slow down and yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. You must come to a complete stop, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may need your lane to pass.
You may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot, and they will not see you. The vehicle may also block your escape route if you need to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across in your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad tracks in your lane. Turning to cross at a different angle may move you into another lane and cause a crash.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You must release the rear brake immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can usually keep it locked. Your motorcycle will stay under control as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: Before riding, what should a working clutch feel like?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if someone else makes a mistake. This safety cushion is not about having more time to accelerate.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you only use the rear brake, you may not learn how to use the front brake properly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
It can create a safety hazard for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet will not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane helps a car driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent side mirror use.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: With their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
As far forward as possible without crowding the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: As far forward as possible without crowding the rider.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger to do on your motorcycle?

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move unnecessarily while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield to you.
Move to a position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Why should you not rely only on your mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: You need to stay aware of your surroundings. Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as other vehicles' horns. Use your horn when appropriate, but do not rely on it for safety.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a conflict with another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: The greatest chance of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles happens at intersections.

questions.question: If you must shift gears while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Use shifting to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before turning. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause a skid.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go first.
Drive through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time?

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most motorcycles are the same, so you don't need to check safety features.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride, check the safety and maintenance. Find where everything is located. Then practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you on a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in your lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation.

questions.question: What type of gloves should you wear when riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Full-fingered gloves
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They improve your grip and protect your hands in case of an accident.

questions.question: Which statement about motorized scooters is true?

options.text: They can only be operated during the day.
They can be operated without a driver license.
They can be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.
